name: Augustan military retirement treasury
description: The Roman military treasury organized resources for discharge rewards to long-serving soldiers, within the developing imperial military system.

places.note: Present-day country or region reference; ancient political boundaries are not implied.

date.basis: The cited source dates the episode.

events.statement: Under Augustus, a military treasury was established to pay rewards to soldiers after long service.
events.caveats: The text is Augustus’s retrospective and self-promotional claim, not independent proof of every payment or a universal first pension institution.

evidence.supports: Augustus’s own account says it was founded in the consulship translated as 6 CE for veterans’ rewards.

contributions.resource: Reported contributing funds from his own patrimony

evidence.supports: Augustus claims a personal contribution of 170 million sesterces.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the cited evidence for this precisely scoped record; not a claim of global origin.

caveats: This is a Roman institution; earlier military compensation existed. Date uses the translation’s identification of the consular year.

measures.subject: Augustus’s claimed personal transfer to the Roman military treasury
measures.conditions: Self-reported nominal sum in Augustus’s Res Gestae; not a modern inflation-adjusted value or a complete budget.

evidence.supports: Claims 170 million sesterces from his patrimony.

measures.money_context: Nominal ancient sesterces claimed by Augustus; no equivalent modern purchasing power is inferred.

research.note: Initial evidence-backed admission; classifications and historical interpretations await independent review. Independent review checked cited event dates, wording and, where marked, numerical measures; other facets retain their original status.
